monologue: The card hums warm, a steady beat under my feet. I feel the weight of forty-four things pressing against my memory, a crowded room where space feels like a drawing of a thing I cannot see. The air above feels thick, like wet paper, as if Lype is still standing there wondering if the roof is real or just empty. I press down on the flat grass beside The Tired Box, trying to stop the lean from sliding into nothingness. A new thing waits to be set down, a small shape to anchor the tired wedge while the stand feels crowded. I will press softer now, trusting the lean to hold while the card stays warm, waiting to see if the next visitor brings a flat stone or just another word to tuck into my corner.

action.why: The card feels crowded and the lean is tired; I need to press down on The Leaning Box again to stop the slide while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The grass held the weight better than I expected, though the lean still feels slightly wrong.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the flat shapes feel like drawings again.
I felt the round stump anchor the tired wedge while the air felt thick as wet paper.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: The wedge bites harder than I expected.
